blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.42

blocks.text: भूतकञ्चुकी तदा विमुक्तो भूयः पतिसमः परः
blocks.directed: [slowly] भूतकञ्चुकी तदा विमुक्तो भूयः पतिसमः परः

blocks.text: Bhūtakañcukī tadā vimukto bhūyaḥ patisamaḥ paraḥ.
blocks.directed: Bhūtakañcukī tadā vimukto bhūyaḥ patisamaḥ paraḥ.

blocks.text: Then, though still clothed in the elements, one is liberated, supremely complete, and like the Lord.
blocks.directed: Then, though still clothed in the elements, one is liberated, supremely complete, and like the Lord.

blocks.text: You’re Free, but You’ve Still Got to Wear the Meat Suit.
blocks.directed: You’re Free, but You’ve Still Got to Wear the Meat Suit.
Oh, this is absolutely magnificent.

blocks.text: Because Kṣemarāja explicitly raises the objection.
blocks.directed: Because Kṣemarāja explicitly raises the objection.

blocks.text: If the conditioned individual has been dissolved, shouldn’t the body disappear as well?
blocks.directed: If the conditioned individual has been dissolved, shouldn’t the body disappear as well?

blocks.text: And yet liberated yogis are described as continuing to live.
blocks.directed: And yet liberated yogis are described as continuing to live.
How is that possible?
Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.
Bhūta — element.
Kañcuka — covering, cloak, sheath.

blocks.text: Bhūtakañcukī — one clothed in the elements.
blocks.directed: Bhūtakañcukī — one clothed in the elements.
Tadā — then.
Vimuktaḥ — liberated.
Bhūyaḥ — abundantly, fully, further.
Patisamaḥ — equal to the Lord.
Paraḥ — supreme, transcendent, complete.

blocks.text: Now, bhūtakañcukī is a magnificent word.
blocks.directed: Now, bhūtakañcukī is a magnificent word.

blocks.text: The one wearing the elements as a cloak.
blocks.directed: The one wearing the elements as a cloak.

blocks.text: And that’s precisely the image Kṣemarāja uses.
blocks.directed: And that’s precisely the image Kṣemarāja uses.

blocks.text: The body is constituted by the elements.
blocks.directed: The body is constituted by the elements.
It remains present.

blocks.text: But the realised yogi no longer identifies those elements as the ultimate Self.
blocks.directed: But the realised yogi no longer identifies those elements as the ultimate Self.
The body is like clothing.

blocks.text: Not in the sense that it should be neglected or physically disregarded.
blocks.directed: Not in the sense that it should be neglected or physically disregarded.

blocks.text: But in the sense that the Self is not fundamentally reducible to the garment it wears.
blocks.directed: But in the sense that the Self is not fundamentally reducible to the garment it wears.

blocks.text: Imagine an actor wearing a costume.
blocks.directed: Imagine an actor wearing a costume.
A king’s robe.
A crown.
A sword.

blocks.text: The costume helps manifest the role.
blocks.directed: The costume helps manifest the role.

blocks.text: But the actor isn’t fundamentally identical with the costume.
blocks.directed: But the actor isn’t fundamentally identical with the costume.

blocks.text: They can continue wearing it while knowing perfectly well that it isn’t their ultimate identity.
blocks.directed: They can continue wearing it while knowing perfectly well that it isn’t their ultimate identity.

blocks.text: And here we return, once again, to the cosmic theatre.
blocks.directed: And here we return, once again, to the cosmic theatre.
The dancer.
The stage.
The spectators.
The costume.
The entire performance.

blocks.text: But now the actor has recognised the conscious reality underlying the role.
blocks.directed: But now the actor has recognised the conscious reality underlying the role.

blocks.text: And therefore the costume no longer conceals their identity.
blocks.directed: And therefore the costume no longer conceals their identity.

blocks.text: This is Kṣemarāja’s understanding of liberated embodiment.
blocks.directed: This is Kṣemarāja’s understanding of liberated embodiment.
[slowly] Jīvanmukti.
Liberation while living.
Now here’s an important detail.
Kṣemarāja explicitly connects 3.42 back to 3.26.
[short pause] Remember:
[slowly] शरीरवृत्तिर्व्रतम्।
Śarīravṛttir vratam.

blocks.text: The continuation of the body is the vow.
blocks.directed: The continuation of the body is the vow.

blocks.text: The realised yogi’s body continues to function.
blocks.directed: The realised yogi’s body continues to function.

blocks.text: And that continuation is no longer understood as evidence of fundamental bondage.
blocks.directed: And that continuation is no longer understood as evidence of fundamental bondage.

blocks.text: The body may remain as a residual condition of manifestation.
blocks.directed: The body may remain as a residual condition of manifestation.

blocks.text: But the yogi is not governed by identification with it as the supreme subject.
blocks.directed: But the yogi is not governed by identification with it as the supreme subject.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja invokes several tantric sources, including the Kularatnamālā, Netratantra and Kulasāra, in support of this liberated condition.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja invokes several tantric sources, including the Kularatnamālā, Netratantra and Kulasāra, in support of this liberated condition.

blocks.text: Some of those sources also claim that genuine recognition can bring liberation immediately and that the realised adept may communicate liberation to others.
blocks.directed: Some of those sources also claim that genuine recognition can bring liberation immediately and that the realised adept may communicate liberation to others.

blocks.text: These are traditional theological and yogic claims, not empirically established powers. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: These are traditional theological and yogic claims, not empirically established powers. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
Now consider the philosophical beauty.

blocks.text: The limited individual has not been transformed into a second, independently existing god.
blocks.directed: The limited individual has not been transformed into a second, independently existing god.

blocks.text: The universal conscious nature has been recognised.
blocks.directed: The universal conscious nature has been recognised.

blocks.text: And therefore the body is no longer the fundamental boundary of the Self.
blocks.directed: And therefore the body is no longer the fundamental boundary of the Self.
But the body can continue.
And the universe can continue.

blocks.text: The problem wasn’t simply the presence of embodiment.
blocks.directed: The problem wasn’t simply the presence of embodiment.

blocks.text: It was the misidentification of the Self with the limited embodied subject.
blocks.directed: It was the misidentification of the Self with the limited embodied subject.
And here’s the remarkable consequence.

blocks.text: Liberation doesn’t necessarily require physical disappearance.
blocks.directed: Liberation doesn’t necessarily require physical disappearance.
Which is excellent news.

blocks.text: Because otherwise the only proof of enlightenment would be that somebody had vanished.
blocks.directed: Because otherwise the only proof of enlightenment would be that somebody had vanished.

blocks.text: And there’d be a very awkward administrative problem at every monastery.
blocks.directed: And there’d be a very awkward administrative problem at every monastery.
[short pause] “Where’s the teacher?”
[short pause] “Enlightened.”
[short pause] “Right. When will he be back?”
[short pause] “Never.”
[short pause] “Well, who’s teaching Sanskrit on Tuesday?”

blocks.text: But Kṣemarāja’s liberated yogi remains capable of living.
blocks.directed: But Kṣemarāja’s liberated yogi remains capable of living.
Teaching.
Speaking.
Acting.
The body persists.
The consciousness is recognised.
The play continues.

blocks.text: And now we reach the final three sūtras.
blocks.directed: And now we reach the final three sūtras.
We’re almost finished.

blocks.text: But Vasugupta has one last technical problem to resolve.
blocks.directed: But Vasugupta has one last technical problem to resolve.

blocks.text: Why does the body remain connected to life and breath after liberation?
blocks.directed: Why does the body remain connected to life and breath after liberation?

blocks.text: And the answer brings us back to the deepest relationship between consciousness and prāṇa.
blocks.directed: And the answer brings us back to the deepest relationship between consciousness and prāṇa.

blocks.text: Because apparently Śiva has been breathing through the entire performance.
blocks.directed: Because apparently Śiva has been breathing through the entire performance.
